questions.question: Which of the following approves the draft framework of the Five-Year Plans?
questions.solution:
• The draft framework of the five-year plan is approved by the National Development Council (NDC).
 
• NDC is the apex body for decision creating and deliberations on development in India.
 
• NDC was set up on 6 August 1952 and it is also known as Rashtriya Vikas Parishad.
 
• The NDC is headed by Prime Minister of India.

questions.question: Mira Seth Committee was related with the development of ________.
questions.solution:
• Meera Seth committee was related to the developments of the handloom industry and it submitted the report in 1997.
 
• This committee had recommended the establishment of national handloom fund of Rs.500 crores.

questions.question: Which amendment act of the Indian Constitution has been called 'mini-constitution'?
questions.solution:
• The 42nd Amendment of 1976 is referred to as the ‘mini-constitution’ as it brought the most widespread changes to the Constitution.
 
• The 42nd Amendment was enacted during the Emergency (25 June 1975 – 21 March 1977) by the Indian National Congress government headed by Indira Gandhi.
 
• The amendment added words like ‘Socialist’, ‘Secular’ and ‘Integrity’ in the preamble, laid down the Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens in Part IV A and made obligatory for the President to act on the advice of the council of Ministers among others.

questions.question: How much time did it take for the creation of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 years 11 months 18 days.**__

 
• It took 2 years 11 months and 18 days to create the constitution of India.
 
• The process was initiated on 9th December 1946 and came to an end on 26th November 1949.
 
• 11 sessions covering 165 days were held in this duration.
 
• Some provision of the constitution came into force on 26th November 1949 while a major part came into force on 26th January 1950.

questions.question: Where was the capital of Gandhara, one of the sixteen Mahajanpadas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Takshashila **__

__
 
• Gandhara was an ancient kingdom situated along the Kabul and Swat rivers of Afghanistan and Pakistan.
 
• The capital of Gandhara was **Takshashila **__also known as Taxila.
 
• __16 kingdoms __were included in Mahajanapadas.
 
• Ancient Buddhist Literature, Anguttara Nikaya text gives the list 16 Mahajanapadas.
 
• They are - Kashi, Kosala, Anga, Magadha, Vajji, Malla, Chedi, Vatsa, Kuru, Panchala, Machcha, Surasena, Assaka, Avanti, Gandhara and Kamboja.
 
• These Mahajanpadas are either Monarchy or a Republics (Ganasanghas).
 
• The important Republics of this period were the Sakyas of Kapilavastu and the Licchavis of Vaishali.
 
• The important monarchical Mahajanpadas of this period were Kaushambi (Vatsa), Magadha, Kosala, and Avanti.

questions.solution:

questions.question: In which of the following states of India bamboo drip irrigation method is prevalent?
questions.solution:
• In Meghalaya, the bamboo drip irrigation method is prevalent in which the tapping of stream and Springwater is done by using bamboo pipes.
 
• In this system, about 18 to 20 liters of water entering the bamboo pipe system per minute gets transported over several hundred meters.

questions.question: Which part of the potato is eaten?
questions.solution:

• The stem of potato is also called the tuber.
 
• Potatoes are rich in fibres, potassium, vitamin C, vitamin B6.

questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT a major component of the biotic environment?
questions.solution:
• The environment can be distinguished into two types:

 
• Biotic environment: consists of living factors in the environment
 
• Abiotic environment: consists of non-living factors in the environment

 
• Plants, animals, decomposers are the living factors which are included in the biotic environment.
 
• Water is a non-living factor hence it is included in the abiotic environment.

questions.question: Through which of the following countries the river Padma flows?
questions.solution:
• River Padma is a major river that flows in **Bangladesh**.
 
• It is the main distributary of the Ganges.
 
• The Padma enters Bangladesh from India near Nawabganj and meets the Jamuna river.
